title: SSE continuity grafting: fragment lineage, semantic-boundary hints, and deterministic toolcall reattach
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients occasionally disconnect mid-stream during long-running generations (multi-minute) or when transient network faults occur. Current resume mechanisms are overly coarse and rarely deterministic when tool/function calls are interleaved with partial structured outputs. Goal: design and implement a lightweight per-fragment lineage scheme and a reconnection handshake that allows clients to graft new fragments onto an existing logical stream, preserve semantic boundaries for structured outputs (JSONL / toolcall frames), and deterministically reattach function/tool call events so downstream consumers do not observe duplicated or truncated tool invocations.

This ticket covers design, API changes (server->client SSE envelope), server-side fragment indexing, minimal on-disk retention for resume windows, client compatibility shims in node/python SDKs, and integration tests + canary rollout. The system must: 1) be backward compatible with existing clients (old clients should still get the stream but without resume benefits), 2) maintain functioncall atomicity (either fully deliver a function call or provide a clear retry path), and 3) keep per-chunk overhead under 12 bytes average beyond payload.

High-level approach: embed a short fragment lineage into each SSE datum: a 64-bit fragment_id + 32-bit seq_in_fragment + a 64-bit parent_fragment_id for grafting (parent may be null). Add an optional semantic hint header ("sem_hint") describing whether the chunk boundary is safe to split for JSON/JSONL/ToolCall tokens. On reconnect clients present the last-acknowledged fragment_id and seq offset; server validates and returns a reconnection token and optional patch sequence to reconcile gaps. For toolcalls, introduce a deterministic reattach token: toolcall events include a call_id (UUIDv7-like) that the server stores in the resume window; when resuming, server ensures toolcall delivery is idempotent by replaying only events whose call_id the client has not previously acknowledged.

Deliverables: (1) API proposal for SSE envelope and reconnection handshake, (2) runtime changes to annotate emitted chunks and retain small resume windows, (3) SDK patches for Python/Node to perform reconnect handshake and grafting logic, (4) integration tests for structured output + toolcall scenarios, (5) canary rollout plan with metrics and alerting (duplicate-toolcall-rate, resume-success-rate, latency p95), (6) documentation and sample migration guide for customers.
acceptance_criteria: API proposal merged to RFC doc in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Continuity+Grafting
Server emits fragment lineage fields for new streams behind feature flag 'sse.grafting'
SDKs (node/python) can reconnect using last ack and resume without duplicating toolcall events in 99% of simulated disconnect scenarios

Integration test harness reproduces scenario: partial structured JSONL stream + interleaved functioncall -> client disconnect mid-toolcall -> reconnect -> final state equals single invocation semantics
Canary metrics show resume-success-rate >= 98% and duplicate-toolcall-rate < 0.1% on test cluster
Backward compatibility: legacy clients continue to receive SSE stream with no regressions in p50/p95 latency (<= 5% regression)
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup and proposal. Shared with runtime and SDK leads. Confluence draft created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Continuity+Grafting

2026-03-06 - Maxwell Zhou (runtime): Reviewed; suggested decreasing fragment_id width to 48 bits to trade namespace for payload size. Concern: collision risk across long-lived streams. Action: quantify collision probability for 48/56/64 bits.
2026-03-07 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype in runtime emitter completed (feature-flagged). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12234

2026-03-08 - Design sync: Agreed semantic hints values: 'atomic', 'soft', 'boundary' with definitions in RFC. 'atomic' means do not split; 'soft' indicates likely safe to split; 'boundary' marks explicit logical boundary (e.g., end of JSON object).
2026-03-09 - SDK status: Node SDK reconnection flow landed behind flag sse.grafting in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/457. Python SDK patch underway.

2026-03-10 - Load testing (staging): Resume window retention of 30s per stream resulted in ~2.2% increase in memory usage on median emitter across 512 streams. Decision: default retention 30s, configurable per-deployment. Follow-up: add retention eviction metric.

2026-03-11 - Security review request submitted for storing call_id in resume window (sensitive metadata): https://security.redwood.ai/reviews/SEC-2026-0311 - security flagged retention limits and logging controls; mitigation: encrypt resume index at rest and redact call args in logs.

2026-03-12 - Integration QA: Found edge case where a client that only acknowledges at chunk boundaries could receive duplicate toolcall when reconnect aligns to mid-toolcall chunk. Mitigation: require client to ack toolcall completion by publishing a stable 'call_ack' marker; SDKs to track call_ack client-side. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-13 - Canaries planned: start with internal-only rollout to us-west-2 cluster with 10% traffic; dashboards: /dashboards/sse-grafting-canary and alert: resume-success-rate < 95% triggers rollback.

2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Server PR opened for lineage persistence and reconnection handshake: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12389. Requesting review from Maxwell and Priya. ETA for merge: 2026-03-18.
